featured.title: The Supreme Court Settled Birthright Citizenship. For Indian H-1B Families, the Relief Is Real but Fragile
featured.excerpt: A 6–3 ruling in Trump v. Barbara preserves citizenship for children born to temporary visa holders — but Justice Kavanaugh left Congress a door, and some Republicans are already walking through it.
featured.image_caption: The United States Supreme Court building in Washington, D.C., at dusk
featured.nri_angle: Indians hold 72% of H-1B visas and have hundreds of thousands of American-born children whose citizenship was directly threatened by Trump's executive order — this ruling is the most consequential immigration win for the Indian diaspora in years.
featured.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India's New Army Chief Has a Five-Letter Plan to Reshape the World's Largest Volunteer Force
news.excerpt: General Dhiraj Seth, the first officer from the Armoured Corps to lead the Army in nearly three decades, has unveiled a 'VIJAY' framework centred on AI, drones and soldier welfare.
news.image_caption: General Dhiraj Seth after receiving a guard of honour as the 31st Chief of Army Staff at South Block, New Delhi
news.nri_angle: India's new Army chief will deepen the US-India defence partnership and expand opportunities for diaspora entrepreneurs in India's growing private defence sector.

news.title: An Indian-Origin CEO Just Raised $800 Million to Challenge Big Tech's AI Monopoly

lifestyle-health.title: A Simultaneous Heat Emergency Is Scorching Two Continents — and Millions of Indian Diaspora Are in Its Path
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Europe's deadliest heatwave in years has killed over 1,300 people, and now a punishing heat dome is descending on the US for July 4th. For the 7 million-strong Indian diaspora across both regions, the message is the same: this is not normal summer heat.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: People cool off in a fountain during summer heat in Budapest, Hungary
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Over 6 million Indian-origin residents in the US and UK face record-breaking heat in their home cities, with multigenerational households and elderly family members at acute risk.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: A New Weight-Loss Drug Just Matched Bariatric Surgery — and It Could Change How South Asians Fight Obesity
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Eli Lilly's retatrutide produced 28% weight loss at 80 weeks in the landmark TRIUMPH-1 trial, the first medication ever to rival surgical outcomes — a potential game-changer for a community with the world's highest metabolic disease burden.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: An Ozempic injection pen — retatrutide belongs to the same GLP-1 drug class but targets three metabolic receptors instead of one
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asians carry the world's highest metabolic disease burden relative to BMI — a drug matching bariatric surgery outcomes could transform obesity treatment for the diaspora.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: The Weedkiller in Your Food May Be Rewiring Your Brain Through Your Gut — and the 'Safe' Doses Aren't So Safe
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A wave of new research finds glyphosate — sprayed on wheat, oats, lentils, and most American crops — disrupts gut bacteria, alters brain chemistry, and triggers anxiety-like behavior at doses far below regulatory limits
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Agricultural spraying in a crop field — glyphosate is the world's most widely used herbicide
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: NRIs face high glyphosate exposure through the American food supply — and India's own use of the herbicide on tea, wheat, and lentils means the risk cuts across both food systems
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Medicare Will Now Cover Ozempic and Wegovy for Weight Loss — Here's Who Qualifies and What It Costs
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A new pilot program launching July 1 lets eligible seniors get GLP-1 drugs for just $50 a month, but the fine print matters — and the clock is already ticking.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: An Ozempic (semaglutide) injection pen — Medicare will now cover GLP-1 medications for weight loss (Wikimedia Commons)
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asians face elevated metabolic risk at lower BMI thresholds, and many NRI families are navigating Medicare coverage for aging parents — making this program particularly relevant for multigenerational Indian American households.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: South Asians Have the Highest Heart Disease Risk at 45 — Despite Eating Better and Drinking Less Than Everyone Else
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A decade-long study of 2,700 U.S. adults found that South Asian men and women develop prediabetes, hypertension, and high cholesterol earlier than every other racial group — even though they report healthier diets and lower alcohol use. The researchers say visceral fat and early-life exposures may explain the paradox.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A doctor checks blood pressure during a cardiovascular screening — researchers say South Asians should begin heart health screenings before midlife
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asian Americans face the highest cardiovascular risk of any U.S. racial group by age 45 — a finding that demands earlier screening, lipoprotein(a) testing, and culturally tailored care for the diaspora community.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Walking 10,000 Steps a Day Can Offset a Full Day at Your Desk, a 72,000-Person Study Finds
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Researchers at the University of Sydney found that each increase in daily steps — up to about 10,000 — was linked to a 39% lower risk of death and 21% lower risk of heart disease, regardless of how many hours participants spent sitting. For the millions of South Asian tech workers who log 8-plus hours at a desk, the data offers a clear prescription.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Walking remains the most accessible countermeasure to prolonged sitting, with benefits scaling up to about 10,000 steps per day
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asian tech workers in the U.S. spend 8-10 hours at desks — among the highest sedentary rates of any demographic — and already face elevated cardiovascular risk by midlife. Walking 10,000 steps daily can meaningfully offset the damage.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Americans Are Ditching Multivitamins for Targeted Supplements — and Two of the Fastest-Growing Are Ayurvedic Staples
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A 25-year JAMA analysis of 63,000 adults finds supplement use surging while multivitamin use drops — with turmeric and ashwagandha leading the charge
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Assorted dietary supplements including vitamin D, magnesium, and turmeric capsules
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Turmeric and ashwagandha — Ayurvedic staples in South Asian households — are now among America's fastest-growing supplements, while targeted vitamin D matters disproportionately for NRIs at higher latitudes.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: The FDA Just Cleared an AI Tool That Detects Hidden Heart Disease From a Routine ECG — and South Asians May Benefit Most
lifestyle-health.excerpt: EchoNext, trained on 700,000 ECG records, caught severe heart failure a cardiologist missed — and its clearance could reshape screening for high-risk populations
lifestyle-health.image_caption: An electrocardiogram readout showing heart rhythm patterns
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asians face 2-4x higher coronary disease rates and often develop heart disease a decade earlier — an AI tool that reads hidden cardiac risk from routine ECGs could catch disease years before symptoms appear.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Strength Training Cuts Type 2 Diabetes Risk by Up to 62% — and Consistency Matters More Than Intensity
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A study of nearly 144,000 people over 19 years found that regular weight training — especially when combined with cardio and less screen time — offers powerful diabetes protection that South Asians have extra reason to pay attention to.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A woman performing strength training exercises in a gym studio
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asians are genetically predisposed to insulin resistance and type 2 diabetes at lower BMIs — making the case for strength training even more urgent for the diaspora.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Your Gut Bacteria May Reveal Colorectal Cancer Before Symptoms Appear — and Fiber Could Be the Key to Prevention
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A new study in Cell Host & Microbe has identified a consistent microbial signature linked to colorectal cancer across ages and populations — and lower fiber intake made it worse.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Illustration of the human gut microbiome, increasingly linked to colorectal cancer detection and prevention (Wikimedia Commons)
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Colorectal cancer rates are surging among young adults globally, and NRIs shifting from fiber-rich Indian diets to Western ultra-processed food face particular risk.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: GLP-1 Drugs Like Ozempic Are Now Linked to Smell and Taste Disturbances — and the Implications Go Beyond Food
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A study of nearly 900,000 diabetes patients found that GLP-1 users had an 81% higher risk of smell dysfunction and a 52% higher risk of taste changes — subtle shifts that doctors say are early markers of neurological health.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A semaglutide injection pen — GLP-1 receptor agonists like Ozempic are now linked to smell and taste disturbances in a growing body of research (Wikimedia Commons)
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asians have among the highest GLP-1 prescription rates due to elevated type 2 diabetes prevalence, and sensory loss carries outsized cultural weight in communities where food is central to identity.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Exercise Alone Can Address Six of the 14 Modifiable Risk Factors for Dementia, a New Study Finds
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Researchers at the University of Minnesota say consistent physical activity can prevent or delay up to half of all dementia cases — and a telehealth pilot proved it works even in rural communities with no gym access.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Regular physical exercise is increasingly shown to reduce modifiable risk factors for dementia, including in older adults (Wikimedia Commons)
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asians face elevated dementia risk through high rates of diabetes, hypertension, and cardiovascular disease — making the case for exercise as neuroprotection especially urgent for the diaspora.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk
